indication.text: Topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 12 years of age and older

citations.quote: WINLEVI (clascoterone) cream is an androgen receptor inhibitor indicated for the topical treatment of acne vulgaris in patients 12 years of age and older.

target_moa.text: Clascoterone is a novel androgen receptor inhibitor that competes with dihydrotestosterone (DHT) for binding to androgen receptors in the skin, limiting or blocking transcription of androgen-responsive genes that modulate sebum production and inflammation; however the exact mechanism in acne is unknown.

citations.quote: Clascoterone is a novel androgen receptor inhibitor, with a chemical structure similar to dihydrotestosterone (DHT) and competes for binding to androgen receptors in the skin.
Clascoterone competes with dihydrotestosterone for binding to the androgen receptor to limit or block transcription of androgen-responsive genes and modify specific gene expression (Kircik 2019).
Clascoterone is an androgen receptor inhibitor. The mechanism of action of WINLEVI cream for the topical treatment of acne vulgaris is unknown.

modality.text: Small molecule (steroidal androgen receptor inhibitor); new molecular entity

citations.quote: The active ingredient is clascoterone, a new molecular entity (NME). Clascoterone is a novel androgen receptor inhibitor, with a chemical structure similar to dihydrotestosterone (DHT)
The chemical structure of clascoterone is a steroid with a ketone at C3, double bonds at C4 and C5, and a propanoate ester at C17.

key_safety.text: Most common adverse reactions (7 to 12% of patients) are erythema/reddening, pruritus and scaling/dryness; local skin reactions occurred at similar rates in vehicle-treated subjects (e.g., erythema/redness 12.2% WINLEVI vs 15.4% vehicle; scaling/dryness 10.5% vs 10.4%; pruritus 7.7% vs 8.2%). HPA axis suppression was observed (1/20 adults and 2/22 adolescents).

Cassiopea SpA submitted new drug application (NDA) 213433 for WINLEVI (clascoterone) cream, 1%, for the topical treatment of acne vulgaris under the 505(b)(1) regulatory pathway.
